label: Small sharp woman, grey streaks, cord glasses
prompt: A small, wiry woman of about forty-five stands on her own front step, close to the door, staring straight into a tiny wide lens mounted in the door frame at chest height, because she has just noticed it and is deciding what to say to it. She has a narrow, sharp-boned face with a pointed chin, pale skin with fine lines at the eyes and mouth, thin dry lips pressed together, and one eyebrow slightly raised. Her short hair is cropped and uneven, dark brown with wide grey streaks over the temples. A pair of reading glasses hangs on a faded green cord against a bobbled charcoal jumper, and one hand holds a rolled-up bundle of leaflets and a pen. The picture is the flat, slightly bowed view of a cheap wide lens looking down at her from above: her head looks a touch large, her shoulders sloped, the red brick porch and a wheelie bin curving at the edges. It is a grey damp English afternoon, soft overcast daylight with the sky behind her blown out to white, colours washed and slightly muddy, soft compressed detail and a little noise in the shadows. Nothing is written or drawn over the image: it is only the raw picture itself, with no lettering, digits, icons or frame furniture. Thanks.

label: Tired British Asian woman, lanyard, cardigan
prompt: A tired British Asian woman in her late thirties stands at her front door at dusk and looks directly into the small wide lens set into the door frame above her, her head tilted a few degrees and her mouth flat, caught mid-thought as she realises it is watching her. She has a round, soft, slightly puffy face, warm brown skin with dark smudges under the eyes and a few spots along the jaw, thick straight black eyebrows, and a faint crease between them. Her long black hair is pulled into a loose, low knot with strands escaping across one cheek. She wears an oatmeal knitted cardigan, pilled at the elbows, over a creased blue shirt, and a council lanyard in a washed-out teal hangs round her neck with a laminated card turned face-in so nothing on it can be read; she holds a carrier bag of shopping and a set of keys. The view is steeply from above through a cheap lens, so the edges of the porch bow inward and her feet feel far away. The only light is a yellow street lamp from the left and a hallway bulb leaking round the door behind her, so her face is half orange and half grey-blue, the dark parts crushed and grainy, colours drained and smeared by heavy compression. The frame holds only the scene itself, with no writing, numbers, symbols or overlays of any kind. Thanks.

label: Big freckled red-faced woman, old fleece
prompt: A big, broad woman of about fifty-five stands square in front of her door on a freezing morning and stares straight up into the small wide lens set in the door frame, chin lifted, one eyebrow down, having obviously spotted it and taken it personally. She is tall and heavy-set with wide shoulders and a thick neck. Her large round face is flushed raw red from the cold across the cheeks and nose, thickly freckled over pale skin, with broken veins at the nostrils, a double chin, deep lines either side of a wide mouth, and chapped lips. Her ginger hair has faded to sandy and white at the front and is flattened under a hairband that she has pushed back, leaving a frizz of loose wisps. She wears an old, bobbled forest-green walking fleece with a zip pulled up to the chin and a sagging collar, a rip at one cuff mended with black thread, and muddy boots with the laces undone. The picture comes from above through a cheap lens, so she looms and the porch tiles curve away. Low winter sun from behind the camera side glares off her wet face and the white painted door; frost sits on a doormat, the whites are clipped, the colour is thin and chalky, and fine noise crawls in the dark areas. There is nothing written, drawn or displayed on the image, no letters, numbers or interface; it is only the picture. Thanks.
